title: Effectiveness of implementation of exhaled breath aerosol sampling to screen for respiratory infections in migrant populations
summary:
Respiratory infections are a leading cause of health problems among refugees and migrants. Testing for the presence of respiratory infections, including tuberculosis, is important in order to identify the cause and initiate appropriate management. Current diagnostic methods are limited by difficulty in sample collection and accuracy of pathogen detection. 

Human breath is an easy to obtain and non-invasive sample, and offers promise as a sample type for respiratory infection diagnostic tests. This study will compare two different breath collection devices for screening and diagnosing tuberculosis and viral respiratory infections among migrants arriving in Italy and Germany. The study will look at how feasible, acceptable, and useable the breath collection devices are.  

Migrants in arrival centers will be screened for inclusion in the study. They will be divided by the presence of respiratory symptoms, and each person will be assigned to give a breath sample using one of the two breath collection devices. The breath collection devices will be used equally within this study. All participants will be offered the usual care and testing for respiratory infections provided by the clinic as per local guidelines. Breath samples will be tested for respiratory pathogens by PCR.  We will assess how often viruses or TB are detected, look at how many tests are successfully completed with each device, look at how many participants found the device easy to use, investigate which device they prefer to use and why, and understand how the breath tests compare to current diagnostic tests.

Respiratory tuberculosis, not confirmed bacteriologically or histologically
Acute upper respiratory infections of multiple and unspecified sites

interventions.name:
Participants will provide a breath sample using blowtube-based breath collection device. Samples will be tested for respiratory viruses and tuberculosis using multiplex molecular platforms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Individuals hosted in migrant arrival centers.
Able and willing to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who have completed active TB treatment within the past 12 months. 
Individuals who are currently undergoing treatment for active or latent TB.
